decks.domain: Insurance, financial responsibility, crash duties and the driving record

cards.front: What insurance must every registered vehicle in Nevada carry?
cards.back: All Nevada motorists must comply with mandatory insurance and financial responsibility laws, and every registered motor vehicle in the state must be covered by liability insurance.

cards.front: When do Nevada's minimum liability amounts apply?
cards.back: Nevada law sets minimum liability insurance amounts that apply whenever you drive or own a vehicle in the state.

cards.front: How must you be able to show proof of insurance?
cards.back: Keep the insurer's Evidence of Insurance Card in the vehicle, or have it ready in electronic form to show on a mobile device.

cards.front: What are Nevada's minimum liability limits for injury or death?
cards.back: Nevada's minimum liability coverage is twenty-five thousand dollars for injury or death of one person in a crash and fifty thousand dollars for injury or death of two or more people in one crash.

cards.front: What is Nevada's minimum liability limit for property damage?
cards.back: Nevada's minimum liability coverage also includes twenty thousand dollars for damage to or destruction of other people's property in any one crash.

cards.front: What does the NV LIVE program do?
cards.back: NV LIVE, the Nevada Liability Insurance Validation Electronically program, works with licensed insurers to flag registrations whose insurance has ended or lapsed.

cards.front: What do you pay if your registration is suspended for an insurance lapse?
cards.back: If a registration is suspended for an insurance lapse with no replacement coverage for that period, you pay a reinstatement fee plus fines starting at two hundred fifty dollars and reaching up to one thousand seven hundred fifty dollars for each vehicle on that policy.

cards.front: Do lapse fines apply once or for each vehicle on the policy?
cards.back: Lapse fines and the reinstatement fee apply to each registered vehicle that the lapsed policy covered.

cards.front: What other penalties can follow an insurance lapse?
cards.back: Further penalties for an insurance lapse can include an SR-twenty-two requirement, a thirty-day driver license suspension, or both.

decks.domain: Insurance, financial responsibility, crash duties and the driving record

cards.front: How does a police-investigated crash reach the DMV?
cards.back: When law enforcement investigates a crash, the officer sends your insurance information and a description of the damage or injuries to the DMV.

cards.front: When must you file an SR-one, and how soon?
cards.back: If police do not investigate a crash that causes seven hundred fifty dollars or more in damage or injures anyone, you must send a Report of Crash Form, the SR-one, to the DMV within ten days.

cards.front: How does crash reporting differ when police investigate and when they do not?
cards.back: A police-investigated crash reaches the DMV through the officer's report, while a crash without police investigation that injures anyone or causes seven hundred fifty dollars or more in damage needs your own SR-one within ten days.

cards.front: Who must complete the SR-one, and where do you get it?
cards.back: The SR-one must be completed by anyone who was the driver or the registered owner of a vehicle in the crash, and the form is available at DMV offices, the Nevada Highway Patrol, local police and the DMV website.

cards.front: What does the DMV Financial Responsibility Section decide after a crash?
cards.back: After a crash, the DMV Financial Responsibility Section decides who was at fault, whether every vehicle and driver was insured, and the total liability.

cards.front: What can happen to an at-fault driver without liability insurance?
cards.back: An at-fault driver without liability insurance may have the license or registration suspended, must post a deposit with the DMV to cover crash costs, or must arrange payment with the other parties.

cards.front: What can happen if you fail to report a crash to the DMV?
cards.back: Failing to report a crash to the DMV can lead to suspension of your driver license, your vehicle registration, or both.

cards.front: What is an SR-twenty-two?
cards.back: An SR-twenty-two is liability insurance on a driver license that lets the DMV monitor the insurance of a suspended or revoked driver through reports from the insurer, and it may be required for reinstatement.

cards.front: When does SR-twenty-two coverage start, and when should you buy it?
cards.back: SR-twenty-two coverage starts when you actually reinstate, you file the form only once, and you should not buy it until every other reinstatement requirement is met.

cards.front: How do the SR-one and SR-twenty-two differ?
cards.back: The SR-one is a crash report you file, while the SR-twenty-two is proof-of-insurance coverage that the DMV monitors when reinstating a suspended or revoked driver.

cards.front: What decides the cost of SR-twenty-two coverage?
cards.back: The price of SR-twenty-two coverage depends on how the insurance company structures it.

decks.domain: Insurance, financial responsibility, crash duties and the driving record

cards.front: What are the first duties at a crash scene?
cards.back: At a crash, stop, get medical help for anyone injured, warn traffic and notify law enforcement.

cards.front: What should you do after a fender bender with no injuries?
cards.back: In a fender bender with only property damage and no injuries, move the vehicle if it can be moved safely to a spot that does not block traffic, then return to the scene.

cards.front: How do the first steps differ for an injury crash and a fender bender?
cards.back: If a crash involves injuries, the first duties are to stop, get medical help and warn traffic; the move-it-aside rule covers a fender bender with property damage only and a vehicle that can be moved safely.

cards.front: What information must you exchange with other drivers after a crash?
cards.back: Exchange your name, address, driver license number, registration and insurance information with every other driver involved.

cards.front: What must you do after hitting an unattended vehicle or property?
cards.back: If you hit an unattended vehicle or other property, give the owner your name, address, license number, registration and insurance details, in person or in a note left behind.

decks.domain: Insurance, financial responsibility, crash duties and the driving record

cards.front: Why can a Nevada driver license be suspended, revoked or canceled?
cards.back: A Nevada driver license is a privilege, and it can be suspended, revoked or canceled if you stop driving safely and obeying the rules.

cards.front: What goes on your Nevada driving record?
cards.back: Crashes and traffic convictions go on your driving record, including violations committed in other states.

cards.front: How long do most violations and DUI convictions stay reportable?
cards.back: Most violations can be reported to your insurer for three years, while convictions related to driving under the influence stay on the record for seven years.

cards.front: Which stays longer on your record, most violations or a DUI conviction?
cards.back: Most violations stay reportable to insurers for three years, while DUI-related convictions stay on the record for seven years.

cards.front: When are demerit points added, and over what period are they counted?
cards.back: Every traffic violation carries demerit points, added once a court sends the DMV notice of a conviction or civil infraction, and points are counted over a twelve-month period.

cards.front: How many demerit points in twelve months lead to suspension?
cards.back: Receiving twelve or more demerit points in any twelve-month period means your license will be suspended.

cards.front: How can traffic school help with demerit points?
cards.back: With three to eleven points, completing a DMV-approved traffic safety course removes up to three points, but only once in any twelve-month period, and the conviction itself stays in your driving history.

cards.front: When are traffic school points actually removed?
cards.back: Points from traffic school are removed only when the school reports your completion for credit, and the DMV will notify you if unsafe driving puts your license status in jeopardy.

cards.front: What happens after a conviction for a major offense such as DUI?
cards.back: A conviction for a major offense such as DUI or causing substantial bodily harm revokes the license; these offenses carry no demerit points.

cards.front: How does points-based suspension differ from revocation?
cards.back: Points-based suspension comes from reaching twelve points within twelve months, while revocation follows a single major conviction such as DUI that carries no points at all.

decks.domain: Insurance, financial responsibility, crash duties and the driving record

cards.front: How many points do reckless driving, careless driving and failing to aid carry?
cards.back: Demerit points: reckless driving is eight points, and careless driving or failing to give information or render aid at a crash scene is six points.

cards.front: Which carries more points, reckless or careless driving?
cards.back: Reckless driving carries eight demerit points while careless driving carries six.

cards.front: Which common violations carry four points each?
cards.back: Demerit points: following too closely, failing to yield the right-of-way, failing to yield to a pedestrian, and disobeying a traffic signal or stop sign are four points each.

cards.front: Which violations carry two points each?
cards.back: Demerit points: impeding traffic or driving too slowly, failing to dim headlights, and a prima facie speed violation or driving too fast for conditions are two points each.

cards.front: How do the points for driving too fast for conditions compare with speeding?
cards.back: A prima facie speed violation or driving too fast for conditions costs two points, the same as speeding eleven to twenty miles per hour over the limit.

cards.front: How do speeding points rise with speed over the limit?
cards.back: Speeding points rise with speed over the limit: one to ten miles per hour over is one point, eleven to twenty is two points, twenty-one to thirty is three points, thirty-one to forty is four points, and forty-one miles per hour or more is five points.

cards.front: Is the handbook's point list complete, and do commercial drivers face more?
cards.back: The point list is only partial, and holders of a commercial driver license may face extra penalties and points for some violations.

cards.front: What can a free online DMV account show you?
cards.back: A free online account through the DMV website shows license status and expiration, a driver history printout, and full lists of demerit points, violation codes and court details.

cards.front: What license misuse is illegal in Nevada?
cards.back: It is illegal to give false information on a Nevada license application, to alter your license, to lend it to anyone, or to use another person's license.

recap_hooks.text: Every registered vehicle needs liability insurance, with proof in the car or on your phone.
The minimums are twenty-five thousand dollars for one person, fifty thousand for two or more, and twenty thousand for property.
If police do not investigate a crash with injuries or seven hundred fifty dollars or more in damage, file an SR-one within ten days.
The SR-one reports a crash, while the SR-twenty-two is monitored proof of insurance for reinstatement.
At a crash, stop, get medical help, warn traffic and notify law enforcement.
After hitting unattended property, leave your details for the owner.
Twelve or more points in twelve months means suspension.
Traffic school removes up to three points once a year, and major offenses like DUI revoke the license.
Reckless driving is eight points and careless driving six.
Speeding points rise from one to five as your speed over the limit grows.
